education.quote:
How are we doing it?

🍎 $9,600 for student teachers through the MI Future Educator stipend
✏️ $10,000 scholarships for future educators under the MI Future Educator Fellowship
💸 $150 million in educator bonuses

I'll always be proud to support our up-and-coming educators.
Hardworking teachers are the bedrock of our schools – that’s why we’re lowering costs and reducing barriers to ensure that everyone who wants to be a teacher can be.

We want our teachers to do what they do best: help every kid in Michigan succeed.  That means investments in teacher development, classrooms where kids can stay focused with free meals and no phones, and a curriculum that’s proven to help students thrive.

If you’d like to find a summer meal site near you or learn more about the program, just visit mcgi.state.mi.us/schoolnutri….

Let’s keep working together to help kids learn, grow, and enjoy their summers.
Last summer alone, nearly 9 million meals were served to Michigan kids. That’s millions of opportunities for children to stay healthy, active, and ready for what comes next.

Here in Michigan, we’ve made a simple promise: no child should have to learn on an empty stomach.

That’s why in this year's budget, we're continuing to fund free breakfast and lunch for all 1.4 million public school students.

A strong education is the foundation of a successful future. I'll always be proud to support Michigan's students and educators. 
  
Together, we’re investing in our students and creating a better, brighter future for all.￼

Here's how we're using it: 
  
☀️ Improving early starts with free pre-k for all 4-year-olds 
  
📚 Reinforcing proven methods with LETRS training, literacy coaches, and science of reading
🤝 Expanding extra help programs through tutoring and out-of-school programming￼

In my State of the State Address earlier this year, I laid out a comprehensive plan to improve literacy across the state.  
   
Today, I was proud to sign a bipartisan education budget that invests the most funding dedicated to literacy in state history.￼
